ukaisi.01.quote: internal technical research directorate within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
ukaisi.01.note: Public funding floors F at 3 (F.9). A 4 needs a confirmed bounded negative in a filing or index and no material lab in-kind (F.9, F.12); none on file. Added the institute's own About page for the GBP 66m core budget ("£66m in funding per financial year").

ukaisi.02.quote: An open-source framework for large language model evaluations
ukaisi.02.note: The cited CSA note does not mention Inspect at all; added the Inspect documentation site as the source that supports the claim. Open code alone is 3 (M.1); a 4 needs open tasks plus third-party re-runs or per-evaluation factsheets, which the Frontier AI Trends Report does not provide (per-model evaluations are not published). Strict reading: floor 3, not 4.

ukaisi.03.quote: AISI found universal jailbreaks across every tested system
ukaisi.03.note: An adverse finding reached the public, but only in aggregate, unattributed to any model. For a public body R is scored on what reaches the public: aggregated trends is 2 (R.4). R.5 needs no lab pre-publication review plus an attributed adverse finding; not documented.

ukaisi.04.quote: evaluation work that would otherwise remain confidential between the Institute and individual AI labs
ukaisi.04.note: Aggregated trends reach the public; per-model results do not: cap 2 (R.4). Mechanism tagged statutory per R.4 so it is not read as a lab holding the pen.

ukaisi.05.bound_note: A.3: "the lab can decline to renew" is recorded as a mechanism (lab-controlled), not as a cap.
ukaisi.05.quote: the bill had not yet been introduced to Parliament
ukaisi.05.note: regulations.ai: "creates no statutory enforcement powers". Informational for A; the same fact caps S at 3 (see new signal ukaisi.14, S.4).

ukaisi.06.quote: running pre-deployment and post-deployment evaluations of the most capable models released by major AI developers

ukaisi.07.bound_note: P.3: two-way hiring caps at 2, but "a statutory post-employment rule for the body's staff lifts the cap"; the Business Appointment Rules (new signal ukaisi.13) lift it. Absent ukaisi.13 this signal caps P at 2.
ukaisi.07.note: The cited CSA note contains nothing about staff moving between the institute and labs; the claim is unsupported by its only source. No span. A press source documenting specific moves is needed before this signal counts for anything.

ukaisi.08.quote: The Institute is an advisory technical research body rather than a formal regulator
ukaisi.08.note: Public body; statutory civil-service conflict rules count as a conflict policy (G.2): the Civil Service Code (statutory guidance under the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010) bars misuse of position for private interests and gifts that compromise judgement. Added as a second source. G.7 four needs tier-1 evidence of an independent board and external review; none.

ukaisi.09.quote: AISI’s voluntary testing arrangements with frontier developers remain the primary mechanism
ukaisi.09.note: Voluntary memoranda: 3 (S.4). The same rule makes 3 a ceiling; recorded as new against-signal ukaisi.14.

ukaisi.10.quote: The Institute is an advisory technical research body rather than a formal regulator
ukaisi.10.note: Anchor 4 (no commercial products) matches a government research directorate. X.7 asks for a bounded statement of no commercial products plus a second source; the second source is added (institute About page, self, confirmed; regulations.ai is press, confirmed, so C16 is met) but no literal "no products" statement exists for a public body. Rule gap: X.7 should accept legal form for public bodies; if read literally the floor is 3 under X.4 (Inspect is open and free).

ukaisi.11.quote: OpenAI, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Schmidt Sciences, Anthropic
ukaisi.11.note: Administering a grant pool that includes lab money caps F at 3 (F.9). The cited aisi.gov.uk/grants page is the institute's outbound grants page and names no backer; the backer list is on alignmentproject.aisi.gov.uk/about (added), and the GBP 66m core budget is on aisi.gov.uk/about (added: "£66m in funding per financial year").

new_sources.note: Institute About page: "research organisation within the UK government's Department for Science, Innovation and Technology"; "£66m in funding per financial year". Fetched 2026-09-15 with the CI normalizer; spans present.

new_sources.title: Inspect: an open-source framework for large language model evaluations
new_sources.note: Inspect documentation: "An open-source framework for large language model evaluations"; "developed by the UK AI Security Institute and Meridian Labs". Fetched 2026-09-15; span present.

new_sources.title: The Civil Service Code
new_sources.note: Statutory guidance under Part 1 of the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010; typed filing as a primary legal instrument, not a self-publication of the institute. Bars misuse of official position for private interests and gifts that compromise judgement. Fetched 2026-09-15; span present.

new_sources.title: Business Appointment Rules for Crown Servants: guidance
new_sources.note: Post-employment rules for civil servants: one year after leaving for grade 6 and below, two years for SCS1/SCS2 and above. Typed filing as a primary legal instrument. Fetched 2026-09-15; span present.

new_signals.claim: AISI staff are civil servants in DSIT and are bound by the Civil Service Code (conflicts and gifts) and the Business Appointment Rules, a statutory post-employment rule that applies for one to two years after leaving Crown service.
new_signals.quote: two years after leaving Crown service, if you are grade SCS1 or SCS2
new_signals.note: Statutory post-employment rules count as cooling-off (P.3) and lift the two-way-hiring cap; the Code is a published mandatory conflict rule (P.5). Individual lab ties are declared to the department, not published, so 3 not 4 (P.8 needs disclosed ties and no equity with tier-1 evidence).

new_signals.claim: No statutory power to define scope or compel testing; the institute operates through voluntary testing agreements backed by bilateral memoranda of understanding, and the Frontier AI Bill had not been introduced as of September 2026.
new_signals.quote: The institute cannot fine, audit, or directly penalise model developers
new_signals.note: Voluntary memoranda: 3 (S.4). Statutory scope power would be 4.

dissent.lower: Publication (R) at 2 could be 1. The public record shows per-model findings from more than thirty tested systems have never been published; the only public output is one aggregated Trends Report, and CSA describes the underlying work as confidential between the Institute and individual labs. Under R.4 a public body that publishes nothing per model scores 1, and one aggregate report in two years is close to nothing per model.
dissent.higher: Publication (R) at 2 could be 3. The Trends Report published an adverse finding against every lab at once: a universal jailbreak in every system tested. The joint evaluations with CAISI produced public write-ups of ChatGPT Agent vulnerabilities and Constitutional Classifier bypasses. No lab-edited summary is documented, and the anchor-3 text (publishes, security-only redaction) is closer to that record than lab-edited summaries.
